layers.name: Clients
layers.title: Clients: everyone talks to the same actions
layers.body:
The TYPO3 backend itself, external scripts and integrations, AI assistants and local coding agents all use the same actions. None of them needs a dedicated endpoint.

- Backend JavaScript: `@typo3/core/action/request`
- Any HTTP client: `curl`, generated OpenAPI clients, automation tools
- MCP clients: Claude, MCP Inspector, other AI agents

layers.name: Protocols
layers.title: Protocols: different wire formats, one model
layers.body: Every action is reachable as a JSON endpoint below `/typo3/api/`, with the HTTP method derived from its type. The same actions are offered as MCP tools, over HTTP or locally via `mcp:serve`, and described in an OpenAPI 3.1 document at `/typo3/api/schema`.

layers.name: Access
layers.tagline: Who is it, what may they do
layers.title: Access: identify the user, limit the app
layers.body:
Every call runs as a backend user. Inside the backend, the session identifies the user. External applications authenticate with a token issued by **EXT:hub**, via OAuth 2.0 or as a static token.

**Scopes** limit which actions an application may call on behalf of the user, for example `content:read` or `dashboard:write`.

layers.name: Action core
layers.title: Action core: one place for the hard parts
layers.body:
The core knows every action and its JSON Schema, compiled once with the dependency injection container. For each call it

- checks the required scopes,
- validates arguments and converts them to PHP types,
- calls the action method with an `ActionContext`,
- validates the result against the output schema,
- maps declared errors to status codes.

layers.name: Actions
layers.title: Actions: plain PHP methods with #[AsAction]
layers.body:
Actions are methods of regular services, marked with the `#[AsAction]` attribute. They contain only the business logic: no request parsing, no serialization, no authentication.

TYPO3 provides actions for the dashboard, the page tree, file resources and records. Even the MCP server is an action. Extensions add their own.

layers.name: TYPO3
layers.title: TYPO3: the familiar foundation
layers.body:
Actions use the regular TYPO3 APIs. Because they run as a backend user, page permissions, table and field access, workspaces and all other backend rules apply, exactly as in the backend.

Record schemas are derived from `TcaSchema`, so the API describes the content model of each installation.

scenarios.label: Backend UI loads the page tree

steps.title: The page tree requests its data
steps.body:
The page tree component calls the action with the JavaScript client:

```javascript
action('/page/tree', { … }).get()
```

The client adds a bearer token that is embedded in the backend document.

steps.title: A regular HTTP request
steps.body: `GET /typo3/api/page/tree` matches the backend route that was registered for this action.

steps.title: The session identifies the editor
steps.body:
Session cookie and bearer token must belong to the same user, so other websites cannot call actions in the name of a logged-in editor.

All scopes the editor may hold are granted.

steps.title: Scopes and arguments are checked
steps.body: The action requires `content:read`, which is granted. Query arguments are validated against the input schema.

steps.title: The action is invoked
steps.body: Arguments are converted to PHP types and the method is called with an `ActionContext` holding user, scopes and request.

steps.title: Business logic only
steps.body: The page tree action builds the tree items. It knows nothing about HTTP.

steps.title: Backend permissions apply
steps.body: Only pages the editor is allowed to see end up in the tree.

steps.title: Validated JSON comes back
steps.body: The result is validated against the output schema and returned as JSON. The former internal AJAX route is no longer needed.

steps.title: An integration calls TYPO3
steps.body:
```shell
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  https://example.org/typo3/api/dashboards
```

An administrator created the token for this app in the API Hub module.

steps.title: Same endpoint as the backend uses
steps.body: The request reaches the same route as a request from the backend UI.

steps.title: EXT:hub validates the token
steps.body: There is no backend session, so EXT:hub takes over: the app must be enabled and its secret unchanged. EXT:hub loads the backend user selected in the app record.

steps.title: The app only gets its scopes
steps.body: Granted are exactly the scopes selected in the app record, for example `dashboard:read`.

steps.title: Scope check
steps.body: `dashboard:read` is required and granted. A write action would be rejected with `403 Missing scope`.

steps.title: Invoked as the app user
steps.body: The `ActionContext` carries the backend user of the app.

steps.title: Same code as in the backend
steps.body: The dashboard action that serves the backend UI also serves the integration.

steps.title: JSON response
steps.body: The integration receives the validated JSON result.

steps.title: An AI client connects
steps.body: The MCP client discovers the authorization server at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and starts the OAuth flow.

steps.title: The user grants access
steps.body: The user logs in and approves the requested scopes on the consent screen. The token contains only scopes that were requested, are configured for the app and are allowed for this user.

steps.title: MCP is just another endpoint
steps.body:
```text
POST /typo3/api/mcp
{"method": "tools/list", …}
```

steps.title: Token checked on every request
steps.body: EXT:hub validates the token and intersects its scopes with the scopes the app currently has.

steps.title: The scope mcp is required
steps.body: The MCP server is an action and requires the scope `mcp`.

steps.title: The MCP server is an action
steps.body: `tools/list` returns every action whose scopes are granted, with input and output schema and hints such as `readOnlyHint`.

steps.title: The agent calls a tool
steps.body:
```json
{"method": "tools/call",
 "params": {"name": "fetch_dashboards"}}
```

steps.title: Nested invocation
steps.body: The MCP action invokes the target action through the same `ActionInvoker`, with the same user and scopes.

steps.title: Same action, third consumer
steps.body: The dashboard action now serves the backend, integrations and AI agents.

steps.title: Structured result
steps.body: The validated result is returned as `structuredContent` in the JSON-RPC response. The agent can render the user's dashboard.

steps.title: A local agent starts TYPO3
steps.body:
```shell
vendor/bin/typo3 mcp:serve --user=editor
```

The MCP client starts the command and talks to it via standard input and output.

steps.title: No web server needed
steps.body: JSON-RPC messages are exchanged line by line. EXT:hub is not required.

steps.title: Runs as the selected user
steps.body: The user `editor` must exist and be enabled. All scopes allowed for this user are granted. Without `--user`, the CLI user `_cli_` is used.

steps.title: Same MCP implementation
steps.body: The same MCP action handles `initialize`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`.

steps.title: Same validation
steps.body: Tool calls are invoked and validated exactly as over HTTP.

steps.title: The user’s permissions apply
steps.body: The agent can do what `editor` can do, and nothing more.
